command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
since=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "round" && $4 !~ /^implement#/ { print $1; exit }')
start=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "task" && $4 == "started" { print $1; exit }')
[ -n "$since" ] || since=$(git rev-parse "$start^" 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
changed=$({ git diff --name-only "$since"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
forbidden=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -E '^(openspec/|temporary-docs/|\.gnomish/|\.github/|\.claude/|docs/adr/|CLAUDE\.md$)' | grep -vxF "$change/tasks.md" | grep -v "^$reports/handoff/" || true)
[ -z "$forbidden" ] || { echo "$forbidden"; echo "the implement stage edits only packages/, docs/ outside docs/adr/, the checkboxes of $change/tasks.md and $reports/handoff/ - put changes to these paths into a handoff patch (see .gnomish/stages/specify/handoff.md) and restore the files above with: git checkout $since -- <file>"; exit 1; }
dependencies=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -E '(^|/)(package\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml)$' || true)
if [ -n "$dependencies" ] && ! grep -qiE 'pnpm add|dependenc|package\.json' "$change/tasks.md"; then echo "$dependencies"; echo "tasks.md asks for no dependency or package.json change - restore the files above with: git checkout $since -- <file>"; exit 1; fi

command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
for patch in "$reports"/handoff/*.patch; do
  [ -e "$patch" ] || continue
  git apply --check "$patch" || { echo "$patch does not apply to the branch - regenerate it as .gnomish/stages/specify/handoff.md describes"; exit 1; }
done
if grep -qE '^- H[0-9]+' "$change/tasks.md" && [ ! -f "$reports/handoff/README.md" ]; then
  echo "tasks.md lists handoff items under Human follow-up but $reports/handoff/README.md is missing"; exit 1
fi

findings.message: packages/client/scripts/dataRefresh/cli.ts:30-37 branches on the string literals `command === "verdict"`, `"check-paths"`, `"issue"` (repeated again in USAGE at cliCommands.ts:39-40). .claude/rules/code-style.md: "if a value is used in a `switch`, `if`, or for branching — it must be an enum" / "Are there strings in conditions (if/switch)? → Create an enum". Since the scripts run under type stripping, add an `as const` command object (as REFRESH_SOURCES / REFRESH_VERDICTS / AUTO_SOURCE already do) and use it in both the dispatch and USAGE.

packages/client/scripts/dataRefresh/cliCommands.ts writes the $GITHUB_OUTPUT keys as repeated literals: "title" and "body-file" in both runVerdict (lines 123-126) and runIssue (lines 185-188), plus "verdict", "merge-body-file", "recovery-file". The workflows depend on these keys. .claude/rules/code-style.md: "Is any value repeated in 2+ places? → Must be a constant". Extract an `as const` output-key object.

The readable source names are defined twice: SOURCE_NAMES in scripts/dataRefresh/refreshFailureIssue.ts:8-12 ("zone rules", "city data", "CLDR") and the inline ternary `source === REFRESH_SOURCES.ZONE_RULES ? "zone rules" : "city data"` in scripts/dataRefresh/refreshPullRequest.ts:54-55. code-style.md: "Is any value repeated in 2+ places? → Must be a constant"; glossary.md: one owner per concept. Move the source names into refreshConstants.ts and use them from both files.

findings.message: packages/client/src/test/features/data_refresh/steps/data_refresh_guard.steps.ts has 225 lines; tasks.md says 'Keep every file under 200 lines' and CLAUDE.md says 'Files must stay under 200 lines for AI context quality'. Move the fixture builders (buildCities, buildDataset, buildCommittedCities, releaseOf) to a shared test helper, or split the zone rules scenarios into their own feature/steps file.

packages/client/scripts/dataRefresh/cliCommands.ts has 202 lines, over the same 'Keep every file under 200 lines' limit in tasks.md; move runIssue or the file readers (requireFile/readZoneRulesInputs/readCityData) into a separate module.

scripts/dataRefresh/refreshVerdict.ts rounds the missing-city share to one decimal (PERCENT_DIGITS = 1), so the spec's own case of 61 of 6 000 cities (1.017%, which breaks the 'more than 1%' rule) gives the reason '61 committed cities are missing (1.0% of them)'. That reads as if the threshold was not crossed, which goes against the Refresh guard requirement that the pull request 'state each reason' and against UX1. refreshVerdict.test.ts:54 locks in this text. Show enough precision (e.g. '1.02%') or name the 1% threshold in the reason, and update the test.
